text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- NATO Secretary General Javier Solana will stopover in Budapest today en route to Turkey for a lightning visit and talks with Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti. @
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will lead a trade delegation to Canada on February 9.
- Parliament voted to lift the immunity right of Socialist Party treasurer and MP Laszlo Boldvai yesterday as requested by the prosecutor general, who is investigating the Tocsik affair.
- The three parties on the Interest Coordination Council agreed Tuesday on reforming the pay as you go part of the pension system, but were divided on overall pension.
- Parliament began a debate yesterday on child protection and guardianship. The number of those requiring protection from abuse totalled 313,000 last year, mostly marked by poverty. @
- The Constitutional Court Tuesday struck down several provisions in the tax law that specified tax payment liabilities based on the assumed private use of company cars.
- The Road Fund's revenues should be 50 percent higher than its current income from the tax on petrol, said Transport Minister Karoly Lotz.
- Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik confirmed Tuesday that no mutually acceptable agreement was reached at recent Slovak-Hungarian expert-level talks on the Gabcikovo hydropower plant. @
- Unidentified persons threw two hand grenades into a car dealer's lot in Budapest late Monday night.
- Firefighters rescued 40 residents from a block of flats set ablaze by a gas explosion in Budapest.

- Balazs Novaky, the national commander of the border guards, has ordered a full stock-taking of weapons, after several automatic pistols and other firearms were found Saturday at the home of a border guard officer.
NEPSZABADSAG @

- Russian Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin said he is not worried by the admission of Hungary, Poland or any third state to NATO, but is worried that enlargement of the alliance could unify and mobilise Russian nationalist and militarist forces.
- More energy price hikes are ahead in April, the increase is unlikely to exceed 4 percent.
- Potato producers have asked the Agriculture Ministry to grant them refundable aid, as they may not have enough finances to sow potato seeds this year.
VILAGGAZDASAG @
- A bank syndicate to finance the expansion of Ferihegy Terminal 2 has formed on the London money market, and expects to conclude contracts in 2-3 weeks.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- One-third of MOL shares will be sold according to the original schedule and government decrees, said Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha said.

- The chemical company BorsodChem plans to construct a HUF 1 billion formalin production plant in line with European safety and environmental protection standards, mayors from the Borsod region were told. @
- The National Police are sending out 400 more policemen to patrol public areas of Budapest to improve the state of law and order.
